extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers, magazine editors, and literary researchers
extracted.subtask_description: A bibliographic/yearbook resource listing addresses of American magazines that publish short stories and a Roll(s) of Honor of notable short stories (American and foreign) for a given year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address list scope and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Note. This address list does not aim to he complete, hut is based simply on the magazines which I have consulted for this volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The address list is explicitly limited to the magazines the compiler consulted; users should treat it as a selective, not exhaustive, market list. Do not assume completeness; verify addresses and seek additional markets beyond this list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazines included: publishes short stories
rubrics_metrics.description: ADDRESSES OF AMERICAN MAGAZINES PUBLISHING SHORT STORIES
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only magazines that publish short stories are listed in this section — inclusion is predicated on the magazine being a market for short fiction. Use the list to identify likely publication venues for short fiction submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roll of Honor: nationality restriction (American roll)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note. Only stories by American authors are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Roll of Honor for the American short story yearbook is limited to works by American authors; foreign authors are not eligible for this particular Roll. When using this Roll as a benchmark for 'best' American short fiction of the year, bear in mind the nationality filter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking 'best' stories (asterisk convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: The best stories are indicated by an asterisk before the title of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An asterisk denotes stories singled out by the compiler as of special excellence. Readers and researchers can treat asterisked items as recommended/commended selections from the year; writers may study these as exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index figures indicating prior Roll inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The index figures i, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 prefixed to the name of the author indicate that his work has been included in the Rolls of Honor for 1914, 1915, 1916, 1917, 1918, and 1919 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric prefixes show an author's repeated recognition on prior Rolls of Honor. Use these markers to identify consistently lauded authors and to trace reputational continuity across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of reprints
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only original first-appearance items are counted for the Rolls and listings; stories that are reprints of earlier publications are deliberately omitted. This affects what is considered for 'best of year' recognition and bibliographic completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Roll conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Note. Stories of special excellence are indicated by an asterisk. The index figures... The list excludes reprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foreign short-story Roll uses the same marking conventions (asterisk for special excellence, numeric prefixes for prior inclusion, exclusion of reprints). When consulting the foreign Roll, expect identical selection/notation rules but applied to non‑American (foreign) short stories appearing in American magazines.
